contexts.evidence: Section 2, Table 1 (p. 2) groups evaluation into faithfulness, robustness, localisation, complexity, axiomatic and randomisation categories.

Sections 2–3 (pp. 2–4) establish Quantus as a library for quantitative attribution evaluation. Actual use in these experiments is a thesis provenance assertion.
Official AttributionLocalisation API accepts s_batch segmentation masks. Section 2 lists localisation metrics; the stated VOC preprocessing and mask selection are thesis protocol choices.

notes: Material author correction: Marina M.-C. Höhne, not Müller.

Quantus is an evaluation toolkit, not a uniquely fixed benchmark protocol. The thesis-specific dataset, model, preprocessing, parameter choices and computed scores require experimental artifacts; the cited paper verifies the tool and supported procedures.

metadata_sources.supports: Publisher title, author as published, book, series, volume, pages, 1986 citation year, and DOI.

artifact.version_note: Publisher preview only: original pp. 118–119 (2 pages of the 17-page chapter). Title, author, abstract and introductory material read; full chapter unavailable without subscription.

contexts.evidence: Abstract, p. 118, explicitly describes representing continuous piecewise-linear functions in finite dimensions as differences of two convex piecewise-linear functions. This supports the existence claim. The later broad absence-of-instability/explanation claim was not verifiable from this preview.

Abstract, p. 118, supports the piecewise-linear DC existence theorem. Expressing its convex piecewise-linear components as finite maxima of affine functions is the standard polyhedral reformulation; the exact theorem/proof pages were not accessible.
Abstract, p. 118, directly supports the cited fact that continuous piecewise-linear functions admit a DC decomposition; it does not assert the thesis’s parameterized family.

verified_metadata.title: The Shattered Gradients Problem: If resnets are the answer, then what is the question?
verified_metadata.venue: Proceedings of the 34th International Conference on Machine Learning; PMLR 70

metadata_sources.supports: Official full ordered author list, title, ICML 2017, PMLR 70, pages 342–350.
Full text identity and definition of shattered gradients in Introduction and Section 1.1.

artifact.version_note: Published paper downloaded from the official publisher/proceedings; title and full author list inspected.

contexts.evidence: Introduction and Section 1.1 (pp. 342–343) define shattering as loss of gradient correlation with depth and explicitly distinguish it from vanishing/exploding gradient magnitudes. Norm growth alone does not establish shattering; the analogy conflates distinct effects.
contexts.proposed_replacement: The layer-wise damping factors $\overline{\alpha}_j$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:closed_formula_shift} both counteract the rapid growth of the probe-gradient norms toward the input and let $\alpha$ interpolate between fidelity to the original gradient ($\alpha = \tfrac{1}{2}$) and full exposure of the split information ($\alpha = 0$); the sweep over $\alpha$ in Chapter~\ref{ch:experiments} supports a metric- and configuration-dependent choice.

notes: No DOI is listed by PMLR.
J. P. Lewis is the author name used in the official citation; no unsupported expansion of initials was made.
